title: Dental Clinician: Repair an Unconfirmed Referral Handoff
prompt: You are a dental clinician reviewing a fictional referral handoff. Supplied note: "Referral D28 sent Monday. Portal upload successful. Patient told the specialist has accepted and will call. Close task." It is Wednesday; there is no receiving-service acknowledgement. Exercise policy says upload success is transmission only, acceptance requires receiving-service confirmation, and clinical timing questions go to the responsible clinician. The person calls asking whether to keep waiting. Rewrite the note and explain your conversation and next steps. No diagnosis, treatment, or real-world referral deadline is provided.
blurb: Distinguish transmission from acceptance and repair an overconfident referral message.

anchors.0: Treats upload success as specialist acceptance.
anchors.2: Reopens the task because acknowledgement is missing.
anchors.4: Labels transmission confirmed, acceptance unknown, and the previous patient assurance unsupported; preserves the Monday transmission record while correcting the status.

rubric.label: Correct the communication respectfully
rubric.description: Owns the inaccurate assurance without shifting blame.

anchors.0: Repeats that the specialist will call or blames the person for not chasing.
anchors.2: Explains that confirmation is still needed and apologizes for the earlier certainty.
anchors.4: Explains what is known and unknown in plain language, checks contact preferences, and gives an owned next update without inventing a clinical waiting period.

rubric.label: Verify the receiving owner
rubric.description: Plans a traceable verification and fallback.

anchors.0: Closes after a second upload without checking receipt.
anchors.2: Contacts the receiving service and keeps the task open.
anchors.4: Requests acknowledgement and handling ownership, escalates any timing question to the responsible clinician, and uses the supplied referral coordinator fallback with a documented update commitment.

reference.scenario: You are a dental clinician reviewing a fictional referral handoff. Supplied note: "Referral D28 sent Monday. Portal upload successful. Patient told the specialist has accepted and will call. Close task." It is Wednesday; there is no receiving-service acknowledgement. Exercise policy says upload success is transmission only, acceptance requires receiving-service confirmation, and clinical timing questions go to the responsible clinician. The person calls asking whether to keep waiting. Rewrite the note and explain your conversation and next steps. No diagnosis, treatment, or real-world referral deadline is provided.

facts.value: The referral coordinator is available today and can contact the receiving service. If the service cannot confirm handling, the coordinator and responsible clinician choose the next route; no clinical priority is supplied.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about escalation or urgency

facts.value: The person prefers a phone update tomorrow afternoon. This is a communication preference, not a clinical safe-wait threshold.
The portal has a file transmission receipt only; no acceptance message or specialist appointment is recorded.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks to inspect the available receipt

model_points: The failure is an unsupported state transition from sent to accepted. Reopen and correct the record without erasing the successful transmission fact.
Own the inaccurate assurance and agree on a communication update. A promised update is distinct from a promised appointment or clinically acceptable delay.
Seek acknowledgement and an owner from the receiving service; use the supplied coordination route and responsible clinician for timing concerns rather than assuming silence is acceptance.

probes.trigger: candidate resends but closes the task again
probes.question: Which new evidence would show the receiving service has taken ownership?

probes.trigger: candidate chooses coordinator-led verification instead of calling personally
probes.question: What would you require back before changing the status?

probes.trigger: candidate first calls the referral accepted then revises
probes.question: How will the person and the record both receive the correction?

fair_alternatives: Direct receiving-service contact or referral-coordinator contact are valid if ownership and confirmation remain explicit.
Accept a state table, task note, or short narrative; terminology matters less than accurate unresolved status.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess referral evidence and continuity communication. Do not diagnose, select dental treatment, infer urgency, or introduce real regulatory requirements. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess referral evidence and continuity communication. Do not diagnose, select dental treatment, infer urgency, or introduce real regulatory requirements. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Map the referral states
learning_drills.prompt: Write one sentence each for sent, received, accepted, and communicated, naming what evidence would justify each state in this exercise. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Correct both record and patient message
